explainedBy: The influence diagram starts: the EPA requires New York to add phosphate to its drinking water — the first cause in the chain behind the algae.

storyboard.claim: The EPA required New York to add phosphate to the drinking water.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram opens with its first box: EPA phosphate rule.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hidden web traced in 145 begins to be drawn.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the first hidden variable as the start of a chain.

explainedBy: Cause -> intended effect: the phosphate keeps lead from leaching out of old pipes — a sound public health measure.

storyboard.claim: The phosphate stops lead leaching from aging pipes — a vital health measure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow gains its second box: Lead kept out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One label added: the rule's intended effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the rule had a good reason.

explainedBy: Cause -> hidden effect: the same phosphate water runs through the sewers into Meadow Lake and fertilizes the algae.

storyboard.claim: The phosphate water overflowed into Meadow Lake and fed the algae.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains its third box: Algae fertilizer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The unintended effect is added at the end of the chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: The good rule's hidden consequence.

explainedBy: The map shows a second input: nitrogen running off the highways joins the phosphate in the lake.

storyboard.claim: The phosphate mixed with nitrogen running off nearby highways.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter of what feeds the lake: Phosphate, Highway nitrogen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From one chain to the several inputs the map uncovers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the highway runoff as a separate source.

explainedBy: A third input: coal particles from Sunday barbecues in the park settle on the water and add carbon.

storyboard.claim: Coal from family barbecues in the park settled on the lake, providing carbon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same sorter gains a third bucket: Barbecue coal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One more input added.
storyboard.addedInformation: The most surprising hidden variable.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect summary: a well-meant rule against lead, combined with highways and barbecues, suffocates the fish in Queens.

storyboard.claim: The EPA's good intentions combined with traffic and barbecues to suffocate the fish.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: Stop lead poisoning -> Highways and barbecues -> Fish suffocate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The inputs collapse into one outcome.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the final consequence for the lake.

explainedBy: A true map is a close look that reveals what is hidden — the listener inspects his own decision the same way.

storyboard.claim: A true map exposes hidden connections; now apply it to a hiring decision.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener in an office holding a magnifier, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the lake to the listener's own office.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the magnifier stands for close inspection.

explainedBy: A job interview: the listener (hiring) faces a candidate for a senior role.

storyboard.claim: You are hiring for a senior leadership role and the candidate is in front of you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener talks to a smiling candidate across the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the hiring example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the interviewer-candidate relationship.

explainedBy: The listener reads the candidate's resume — a flat overview, like a satellite photo of the lake.

storyboard.claim: The resume, skills and revenue numbers are only the satellite photo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener now holds the resume page in front of the candidate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same interview; the listener now holds the resume.
storyboard.addedInformation: The resume as the flat, surface view.

explainedBy: The influence diagram of the office begins with the candidate's personality traits as the first cause.

storyboard.claim: You need an influence diagram of your office, not a list of skills.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A new flow opens: Candidate's traits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lake's map is redrawn for the office.
storyboard.addedInformation: Starts the office's cause chain.

explainedBy: Trait -> ripple: an aggressive communication style affects the morale of the junior design team.

storyboard.claim: How will their aggressive style affect the junior design team's morale?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains: Junior team morale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One ripple added.
storyboard.addedInformation: First hidden effect in the office.

explainedBy: A further ripple: their ambition could alter the delicate relationship with the oldest legacy client.

storyboard.claim: Map how their ambition alters your oldest legacy relationship — the unseen ecosystem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains its third box: Oldest client ties.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One more ripple added.
storyboard.addedInformation: The political side of the hire.

explainedBy: The listener searches his own office for hidden variables, as the planners searched the lake for phosphate and coal.

storyboard.claim: Look for the phosphates and barbecue coal in your own office — but is mapping efficient?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener in the office with the magnifier again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the hiring analogy; the challenge follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the lake back to the office.

explainedBy: Back at the Abbottabad compound model, the CIA analysts are ordered to brainstorm wild ways to identify its occupants.

storyboard.claim: In the divergence phase the CIA ordered analysts to find wild ways to identify the occupants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst with notes beside the walled compound model.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the office back to Abbottabad.
storyboard.addedInformation: Returns to the compound as the object of the brainstorm.

explainedBy: The analysts brainstorm 37 schemes around the compound model.

storyboard.claim: They spent time brainstorming 37 crazy schemes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same analyst and model; she now talks, animated.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The brainstorm gets its number.
storyboard.addedInformation: The count of schemes.

explainedBy: One scheme: throw stink bombs over the compound wall — the analyst points at the model's wall.

storyboard.claim: Someone proposed throwing stink bombs over the wall to watch the reaction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst points at the walled model with a wry smile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First of the crazy schemes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Points to the wall the idea targets.

explainedBy: Another scheme for the same compound: loudspeakers broadcasting a voice at it.
noVisual: No loudspeaker in the vocabulary; the callout names it beside the compound.

storyboard.claim: Someone else proposed loudspeakers broadcasting a voice at the compound.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same model; the analyst surprised, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second scheme.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the loudspeaker lives in text.

explainedBy: The hosts judge the scheme absurd, like a bad spy movie — the analyst's wry face beside the model.

storyboard.claim: The voice-demanding-surrender plan sounds like a bad spy movie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same model; the analyst smirks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reaction to the scheme.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the judgment is commentary.

explainedBy: The skeptic's objection: time runs out while analysts chase crazy ideas.

storyboard.claim: Isn't this a massive waste of time and taxpayer money?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumps, worried, beside a running hourglass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The challenge to the brainstorm.
storyboard.addedInformation: Time draining away as the cost.

explainedBy: The deadline pressure: a target might flee at any moment, so there is no time for 37 wild goose chases.

storyboard.claim: With a ticking clock and a target who might flee, you cannot diagram 37 goose chases.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener under a clock, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From wasted time to the deadline.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pressure that argues against divergence.

explainedBy: The skeptic demands that leadership stop mapping and decide now.
noVisual: Commentary; the impatience is carried by the face and pointing gesture.

storyboard.claim: Leadership just has to make a call — isn't mapping just analysis paralysis?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener points firmly, impatient.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection reaches its demand.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: impatience as a face.

explainedBy: A feeling: under pressure the mind wants it over — the listener slumps under the strain.
noVisual: A feeling, not an event; face and callout carry it.

storyboard.claim: Under pressure our brains crave closure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped and worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts explain the reaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the craving is text-carried.

explainedBy: The rule of the divergence room: every idea about the compound gets written down.

storyboard.claim: The divergence phase is crucial; its rule is that no idea is too crazy to write down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst, happy, holding her notes by the compound model.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the skeptic with the room's rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Back to the brainstorm room as the example.

explainedBy: Even the stink-bomb idea goes on the list — the goal is not to execute it.

storyboard.claim: Even stink bombs — the goal is not to execute the crazy idea.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same model; the analyst points at it with a wry smile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rule applied to the craziest idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls the earlier scheme.

explainedBy: The purpose of crazy ideas: jolt the mind out of its default rut so a new idea appears.

storyboard.claim: The goal is to break the brain out of its narrowband default rut.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener surprised, holding a lit lightbulb.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The why behind the crazy ideas.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the lightbulb as the new idea.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: permitting only obvious answers yields only obvious, often flawed solutions.

storyboard.claim: Only sensible answers in the room lead to sensible, deeply flawed solutions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: Only obvious answers -> Deeply flawed solutions.
storyboard.onScreenText: Only obvious answers -> Deeply flawed solutions
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cost of skipping divergence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the mechanism explicit.

explainedBy: The opposite mechanism: exploring 37 crazy paths creates friction that knocks a hidden variable loose.

storyboard.claim: Exploring 37 useless paths knocks a hidden variable loose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: 37 crazy paths -> Hidden variable loose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The contrasting chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Why the wild ideas pay off.

explainedBy: Result: the loosened variable reveals the one unconventional path that actually works.

storyboard.claim: It leads to the one brilliant unconventional path that works.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains: The path that works.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The chain's result added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the mechanism.

explainedBy: The analogy: walking the dirt road instead of the interstate to see the real landscape.

storyboard.claim: It is like taking the dirt roads instead of the interstate to see the landscape.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener walking a country road through woods.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: An image for divergence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the slower, exploring route.

explainedBy: The deed the narrator warns against: grabbing the first plausible plan and running with it leads to failure.

storyboard.claim: If you grab the first plausible plan and run with it, you fail; endure divergence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener grabs a plan page; the phrase is struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The failure mode of locking in early.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the premature grab being rejected.

explainedBy: Widening the map: beyond the two obvious roads a third path appears before you choose.

storyboard.claim: You must widen your map before you choose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fork in the road with a third dotted path to a star.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lesson of the divergence argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book's signature image of a wider map.

explainedBy: Getting a group to actually disagree is rare and hard — the listener's concern.
noVisual: Commentary; face and callout carry it.

storyboard.claim: Getting a group to disagree and brainstorm is incredibly difficult and rare.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped, worried, in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the room where divergence happens.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.

explainedBy: The CEO at the head of the table presents a plan while the listener sits and listens.

storyboard.claim: In a conference room the CEO outlines a new strategic plan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The confident CEO talks with notes; the listener sits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the conference-room scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the boss and the room.

explainedBy: The listener agrees with the boss at once — praise flows back to the CEO.

storyboard.claim: Everyone nods along: great idea, boss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same room; the listener now smiles and speaks up in agreement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The listener's face and body change to agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows instant agreement.

explainedBy: The boss's idea is echoed straight back: the room only repeats him.

storyboard.claim: 'I totally agree. Perfect sense.' The echo chamber.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO points to his plan; the listener cheers it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Agreement escalates to cheering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the dynamic.

explainedBy: The warm bonding: boss and listener celebrate together, fully aligned.

storyboard.claim: A warm, intoxicating bonding feeling: everyone on the same page.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Both the CEO and the listener celebrate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The CEO now celebrates too.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shared warm feeling.

explainedBy: Consensus feels like alignment — but the listener's face turns as the hosts warn it is terrifying.

storyboard.claim: Consensus feels like alignment — but here the psychology gets terrifying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO still celebrating; the listener stops and looks worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The listener's face turns from happy to worried.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the turn.

explainedBy: The warm feeling of instant consensus is dangerous: the boss talks on, unaware, while the listener sees the danger.

storyboard.claim: That warm feeling of immediate consensus is provably dangerous.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The happy CEO keeps talking; the listener slumps, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The listener's worry deepens to fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrast between the cheerful boss and the danger.

explainedBy: Fast agreement is a false face: rapid consensus masks hidden profiles.

storyboard.claim: Rapid consensus is almost always an illusion that masks hidden profiles.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask beside the smirking CEO.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From feeling to the explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The agreement as a false surface.

explainedBy: Hidden profiles: a group's knowledge splits into kinds of people — first, the cognitively central.

storyboard.claim: In any group there are two types of knowledge distribution; some are cognitively central.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter opens with one bucket: Cognitively central.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the explanation of hidden profiles.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the first group.

explainedBy: What makes them central: the same background and the same assumptions as the majority.

storyboard.claim: They share the same education, culture and assumptions as the majority.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sorter gains: Same assumptions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One label added describing the central group.
storyboard.addedInformation: Their defining trait.

explainedBy: The other side: besides the central people with shared information, there are the cognitively peripheral.

storyboard.claim: They hold shared information; but there are also cognitively peripheral people.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sorter gains: Cognitively peripheral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The second group added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the outsiders of the room.

explainedBy: What the peripheral people hold: unique, unshared information no one else has.

storyboard.claim: They hold unique, unshared information no one else has.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sorter gains its fourth bucket: Unshared information.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The peripheral group's asset added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the hidden-profile split.
